IF THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE, EVERY EFFORT WILL BE MADE TO ATTEMPT TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING. TOWARDS THIS END, THE MAYOR WILL ENDEAVOR TO TAKE A BRIEF PAUSE BEFORE ACTION IS TAKEN ON ANY AGENDA ITEM TO ALLOW THE CITY CLERK TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS, AND SHARE ANY E-COMMENTS RECEIVED DURING THE MEETING.

LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.

Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  July 14, 2020
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4 p.m. on July 14, 2020,
in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California;
Mayor Shea presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember:  Farrah N. Khan
  Councilmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor:  Mike Carroll*
  Mayor:  Christina Shea

  * via teleconference

Prior to convening to Closed Session, Mayor Shea announced that the meeting was
broadcast live on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse
Channel 99, and livestreamed online at cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public
health and prevent the spread of COVID-19, the e-comment feature had been extended for
all agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments
through the public comment portion of each item and would be included as part of the official
record and uploaded to the City’s website. She also assured the community that the City of
Irvine was adhering to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and
throughout City Hall by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.
 City Council Minutes  July 14, 2020

  1.  CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Melching announced Closed Session Item No. 1.1, and noted for the

  RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  Mayor Shea reconvened the City Council meeting at 5:06 p.m. City Attorney Melching, on
  behalf of the City Council, announced that no reportable action was taken in Closed Session

  Councilmember Fox led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  •  Commend Mad Engine on its June 27, 2020, "Drive-Up Mask Giveaway" Event

  Mayor Shea presented a commendation to Mad Engine in recognition of its hosting
  of a “Drive-Up Mask Giveaway” event on June 27, as part of its effort to give away
  one million fabric masks for those in need during the COVID-19 crisis.

  Molly, Perry, City Clerk, noted that an e-comment was received by Anonymous
  Resident, who spoke in support of the commendation and expressed appreciation
  to Mad Engine for keeping the community safe by providing masks.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  July 14, 2020

  CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Khan, as the City’s representative to the Orange County Mosquito and
  Vector Control District, provided a brief update of West Nile Virus confirmed in the County;
  and noted that several residents expressed appreciation to Anthony Caraveo, Senior Project
  Manager, for the management of the Capital Improvement Project Campus Drive
  Rehabilitation Project (Project) between University and Jamboree, which is scheduled to be
  completed ahead of schedule later this summer.

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

  •  The application period for the Rental Assistance Program opened on Monday, July
  13, with more than 700 applications received by the end of the day. It is anticipated
  that approximately 2,000 residents will receive assistance through the program. The
  application period will close at 5 p.m. on Friday, July 24. Residents can apply for one
  of two grants, which include a maximum one-time $1,000 grant for assistance with
  lease termination fees, or a maximum one-time $1,000 grant for rental payment
  assistance. The program is funded with federal CARES Act funding that is expected
  to be disbursed by the State of California to the City later this month. For information
  and to apply, visit cityofirvine.org/rentalassistance.

  •  On July 13, the City launched a COVID-19 drive-up testing program for individuals
  who live or work in the City of Irvine. The testing is being done at the Orange County
  Great Park, in partnership with Curogram and multiple laboratories, including local
  Pangea Laboratory. Irvine is the first city in Orange County to provide COVID-19
  testing to those who live and work in Irvine, regardless of symptoms. Approximately
  400 members of the public have been tested so far, with test results arriving up to
  three days after the appointment. This no-cost PCR testing is available by
  appointment only and will take place Mondays through Thursdays from 8 a.m. to
  5 p.m.

  •  Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, the City has been working to provide additional
  support and solutions for Irvine businesses. On May 12, the City Council approved a
  program to allow restaurants to expand their outdoor seating capacity to safely serve
  additional customers. Under the program, restaurants can apply for a special outdoor
  dining permit to temporarily expand their patio seating into common areas such as
  parking lots and public spaces. City staff has already approved 19 areas for expanded
  patio expansions at 24 shopping centers, making it easier for residents to “Dine
  Irvine.” With Governor Newsom’s closure of indoor business operations earlier this
  month, allowing restaurants and retail to expand their capacity outside is critical to
  helping local businesses while ensuring the health and safety of the community. For
  a list of restaurants approved for outdoor dining, visit cityofirvine.org.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  July 14, 2020

  •  Drowning remains the leading cause of death for children one to four years of age,
  and among the top five leading causes for those under the age of 18, both in Orange
  County and in California. Each year, near drowning incidents also result in life-long
  disabilities. This summer, residents are encouraged to take necessary steps to keep
  children safe. Young children are more at risk and can drown in any body of water,
  including a bucket, bathtub, sink, pool, or spa. For information, including effective
  approaches to drowning prevention, visit drowningpreventionoc.org.

  •  Maruchan, a longtime Irvine company, has generously donated funds to the City,
  Irvine Public Schools Foundation, and the Orange County Fire Authority. These
  generous donations reflect the extraordinary character of Maruchan and its long-
  standing commitment to the Irvine community. Maruchan opened its first U.S. plant
  in Irvine in 1978 and has been a corporate leader for decades.

  from the City’s Municipal Code

  00790906-PMPC, A COMMERCIAL MASTER PLAN AND TRANSFER
  OF DEVELOPMENT RIGHTS AT 2400 BARRANCA PARKWAY IN
  PLANNING AREA 36 (IRVINE BUSINESS COMPLEX)

  This item was considered following Council Business Item Nos. 4.3, 4.2,
  and 4.4. See Additions and Deletions.

  Mayor Shea opened the public hearing at 6:28 p.m.

  Tim Gehrich, Deputy Director of Community Development, presented the
  staff report and responded to questions.

  Tim Strader, Jr., Starpointe Ventures on behalf of the applicant, Gemdale,
  provided a brief history of the Irvine Business Complex and an overview of
  the proposed project.

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about why Supporters’ Alliance
  for Environmental Responsibility (“SAFER”) had not paid appeal fees to
